system_node_hint: The node's output is the audio of apps that play to the default output device. Its input is what they hear as the default microphone. While the graph runs, it sets the default devices; after it stops, the previous ones come back
volume_hint: Volume. Double-click the percentage to reset to 100%
delay_hint: Delay relative to the other outputs: plus plays later, minus earlier. Double-click the value to reset it
balance_hint: Balance: towards the left or the right channel. Double-click the value to center it
issue_balance_direct: Balance doesn't apply here: an app or “System” connected straight to an output plays through the system. Connect it through a cable
calibration_hint: Each output plays a short sweep in turn while the microphone listens. Put the microphone where you listen, hold headphones close to it, and don't use the microphone of headphones being measured. The graph's sound is muted meanwhile.
calibration_no_outputs: The graph has no Output nodes
calibration_direct: An app or “System” plays straight into it: its delay can't apply
calibration_unsteady: The tries differ by {spread}: the result may be off. Measure again in a quieter place
calibration_listen_hint: A tick on all outputs at once with these delays: in sync it sounds as one
calibration_need_two: At least two outputs must be heard to compare them
calibration_widen: The delay range of the graph will be widened to ±{range} s
calibration_too_far: The outputs differ by more than {max} s: the delays will be cut at the widest range
error_calibration_not_heard: not heard: turn it up or bring the microphone closer
app_not_running: Not running: devices will be assigned when it starts
app_no_audio: Hasn't opened audio yet: devices will be assigned when it starts playing
graph_running_with_problems: Running, but not everything works: there are problems
find_cables_hint: Adds cables for the device pairs of virtual cable drivers (Virtual Audio Cable, VB-Cable…) found by their properties
cable_output_mismatch: The output doesn't match the input: audio played into “{device}” comes out of “{pair}”
cable_input_mismatch: The input doesn't match the output: “{device}” gives the audio played into “{pair}”
cable_power_on: Cable is on — turn it off
cable_power_off: Cable is off — turn it on
cable_power_mixed: Cable is partly on — turn it fully on
cable_power_none: Nothing to turn on: the cable's devices aren't selected or aren't in the system
cable_in_description: — an output device that apps play into
cable_out_description: — an input device the audio is taken from
cables_empty: No cables yet. A cable is a pair of devices: an output device that apps play into, and an input device the audio is taken from.
cable_deleted_hint: The cable was deleted from the cable list, choose another one
settings_disable_idle_cables: Turn cables off when the graph is stopped
settings_disable_idle_cables_hint: Cables of the running graph are turned on when it starts and turned off after it stops and when the app quits
settings_new_graph_volume_hint: Whether a new graph starts with volume sliders; you can change it later in the graph's options in the graph list
settings_tray_hint: Closing the window hides it to the tray, and graphs keep running. Without the tray, closing the window stops the graphs and quits
settings_autostart_hint: Audio Graph starts in the tray when you sign in; graphs marked in their options start with it
settings_autostart_hint_window: Audio Graph starts minimized when you sign in; graphs marked in their options start with it
settings_autostart_portable: Only the installed app can start with the system: a portable file or an AppImage may be moved or replaced
settings_hide_minimap_hint: The miniature view of the whole graph in the bottom right corner
graph_volume_sliders_hint: On every node of this graph
graph_balance_sliders_hint: Under the volume of inputs, cables and outputs: left or right. While off, this graph's balances aren't applied
graph_delay_sliders_hint: On Output nodes, to shift their sound in time, for example to match speakers to Bluetooth headphones: plus plays later, minus earlier than the other outputs. While off, this graph's delays aren't applied
graph_start_on_launch_hint: The graph starts when Audio Graph starts with the system
graph_start_on_launch_off: Turn on “Start with the system” in the settings first
calibration_open_hint: Measure with a microphone how late each output sounds and set the delays so they play together
graph_import: Import a graph from a file
error_import_not_graph: The file isn't an Audio Graph graph
error_autostart_portable: Only the installed app can start with the system
error_device_control_windows_only: turning devices on and off is only available on Windows for now
error_device_state_admin: Windows didn't allow changing the device state: administrator rights are required
issue_no_default_input: The system has no default input device
issue_cable_no_output_to_app: Cable “{cable}” has no output selected, so its audio can go only to devices, not to apps or the default microphone. Pick the cable's output in the cable list
issue_delay_direct: The delay isn't applied to sound that goes straight from an app or the System node into this device: the system plays it, not Audio Graph. Connect them through a cable
issue_cable_deleted: The cable was deleted from the cable list
issue_no_default_output: The system has no default output device
issue_app_to_internal_cable: Windows sends app audio only to a device, and an internal cable is invisible to the system. Pick a cable from the list for this cable node
issue_device_to_device: These can't be connected directly: audio has to go from an output device to an input device, put a cable between them
issue_internal_cable_to_app: An app listens only to a device, and an internal cable is invisible to the system. Pick a cable from the list for this cable node
issue_loop: Loop: audio would go round in circles. The loop's links don't work until it is broken
issue_default_output_fan_out: There is only one default output device: the system can't send audio to several places. Route it into a cable, and from the cable wherever you need
issue_app_fan_out: An app has one output device: the system can't send its audio to several places. Route it into a cable, and from the cable wherever you need
issue_default_input_fan_in: There is only one default input device. To hear several sources, mix them into a cable and connect the cable here
issue_app_fan_in: An app has one input device. For it to hear several sources, mix them into a cable and connect the cable to the app
issue_system_node_repeated: The “System” node appears in the graph more than once: there is only one default device
issue_app_repeated: “{app}” appears in the graph more than once: an app has only one device setting
issue_default_output_loop: Loop: the default output device is now the input of cable “{cable}”, so the cable's audio would return into itself
issue_cable_into_itself: Loop: the audio of cable “{cable}” would return into itself
issue_app_taken: “{app}” is already routed by the running graph “{graph}”: an app has only one device setting
issue_defaults_taken: The default devices are already set by the running graph “{graph}”
issue_loop_across_graphs: Loop with another running graph: audio would go round in circles through their cables. Some links of this graph don't work until it is broken
error_app_devices_denied: Windows doesn't allow changing app devices: {error}
step_set_app_device: assigning a device to the app
error_device_exclusive: device is used by another app in exclusive mode
error_cable_default_device: a cable can't use the default device
error_graph_deleted: the graph has already been deleted
virtual_cable_hint: While the graph runs, the cable is an output device and an input device with this name: other programs see them too
error_audio_server_lost: the connection to the audio server was lost
quit_app_hint: Graphs stop, and apps and devices return to their previous settings
